# Vendored Three.js runtime

The application never loads Three.js from `node_modules` at run time.  The
files below are the exact ESM build that the production bundle imports
(`vite.config.js` aliases the bare specifier `three` onto
`vendor/three/three.module.js`).

## Provenance

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| upstream project | Three.js (https://threejs.org) |
| package | `three` |
| version | **0.187.0** (exact, pinned in `package-lock.json` and in `vendor/manifest.json`) |
| licence | MIT (see `three/LICENSE` in the npm package) |
| source | `npm pack three@0.187.0` / the `node_modules/three` tree of the locked dependency |
| copied on | `npm install` (the `postinstall` hook runs `scripts/vendor-sync.mjs`) |

## Files

| file | upstream path | used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `three/three.module.js` | `build/three.module.js` | the ESM entry point (`import * as THREE from 'three'`) |
| `three/three.core.js` | `build/three.core.js` | imported by `three.module.js` itself, shipped unchanged |
| `three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js` | `examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js` | the orbit camera control |

`vendor/manifest.json` records the copied file list and is regenerated by the
sync script, so a reviewer can compare the vendored tree against the npm
package byte for byte.

## No runtime network dependency

The vendored files are the only Three.js code the browser loads.  There is no
CDN, no remote ESM import, no remote texture, HDRI, font, audio or API call
anywhere in the application; the star field, the galaxy band, the disc
texture and the ambient drone are all generated procedurally at run time.
